source.check: names as printed in the News-Letter's list of nominations (5 May, read on the block image); votes read on the block image of its results (4 June) and agreeing with the Northern Whig's

note: Triennial election of Down County Council on the 20 single-member county electoral divisions; nominations received by R. J. Dickson, returning officer, at Downpatrick on 4 May 1927. Colonel Sharman-Crawford, chairman for many years, was not nominated. Polls in Castlewellan and Rathfriland on Thursday 2 June 1927, declared at the County Courthouse, Downpatrick, the next day; the other eighteen were returned unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 5 May and 4 June 1927). No party labels are printed, so none are given. Savage; his opponent is printed 'J. C. M'Guinness' in the nominations and 'J. C. Maginnis' in the Northern Whig.
